3. The case of the plaintiffs in short is that Abdul Meah was the original RS recorded owner of the suit land, who died leaving his only son namely, Bazal Ahmed; that the said Bazal Ahmed died leaving behind one wife Mazema Khatun, one son Emdadul Islam and two daughters Nur Nahar Begum and Shamsun Nahar Begum; that the aforesaid heirs of Bazal Ahmed had been in possession in the suit land on due payment of necessary rents and taxes to the Government; that the suit property was put in auction through certificate Case No. 3496/60-61 for arrear rent and on payment of arrear rent by the heirs of Bazal Ahmed, the certificate case came to an end on 16-2-1961; that by a registered kabala dated 28-10-1963 Majena Khatun, Emdadul Islam and Nurun Nahar Begum transferred 24 sataks of land to Reja Mia and Kamal Uddin; that thereafter Majena Khatun, Emdadul Islam and Nurun Nahar Begum by a registered sale deed dated 3-9-1970 transferred 12 sataks of land to Mohammad Mia and thereafter, Raja Meah by registered sale deed dated 24-10-1970 transferred his aforesaid purchased land to Noman; that Kamal Uddin by registered sale deed dated 10-11-1969 transferred 10 sataks of land to Syed Fazal Ahmed and Syed Ahmmed Hoque and thereafter Noman transferred 6 sataks of land to Maklesur Rahman by sale deed dated 22-1-1971; that Noman and Moklesur Rahman by registered sale deed dated 22-7-1978 transferred 12 sataks of land to Nurun Nahar Begum; that thereafter Mohammad Meah Chowdhury by sale deed dated 23-3-1978 transferred 5 gondas, 3 koras of land to plaintiff No. 1; that said Nur Nahar Begum transferred 4 gondas of land to plaintiff Nos. 2 and 3 by sale deed dated 8-2-1979; that Nur Nahar Begum transferred 2 gondas of land to plaintiff No. 4 by sale deed dated 9-2-1979 and the aforesaid Fazlul Ahmad and Aminul Hogue by sale deed dated 10-7-1979 transferred 6 gondas of land to plaintiff No. 5. Thereafter, the heirs of Bazal Ahmad namely Shamsun Nahar, Nurun Nahar, Mayena Khatun, Emdadul Islam transferred rest of their 5 gondas of land to plaintiff No.5 and in this way the plaintiffs have been in possession of the suit land by purchase through several purchase deeds by erecting houses on conversion of the null land into vhiti land on payment of due taxes to the Government. Thereafter, the plaintiffs constructed residential house and tenanted house in the suit land and have been possessing and enjoying the same; that the plaintiffs installed tube well in the suit property and also planted vegetable garden on vacant land; that the defendants have no right, title and possession in the suit land; that during PS operation the PS khatian was wrongly recorded in the name of one Abdul Bashar, who was a Karjakarak of the vendor of plaintiffs and thereafter BS khatian was correctly prepared in the name of the heirs of Bazal Ahmad; that the defendants are powerful men in locality having militant forces; that the defendant Nos. 1-3 by their hired `gundas' tried to illegally evict the plaintiffs and thereupon, the plaintiffs filed Criminal Case; that at the influence of defendants the officer-in-charge of local Police Station arrested the plaintiff No. 5 on 26-8-1980 and created pressure upon the plaintiffs for surrendering possession of the suit land to defendants and thereby the plaintiffs instituted the suit by mentioning cause of action on 6-8-1980 and 26-8-1980; that due to institute of the suit, the powerful defendants during continuation of Martial law regime issued notice to predecessor of plaintiffs SM Kamal Uddin for appearance before the Martial Law Administrator and on appearance before the Martial Law Administrator, who instructed to SM Kamal Uddin to hand over possession of the suit land by making demarcation through a survey knowing Advocate. Since SM Kamal Uddin did not comply with such illegal instruction, he was given a second notice on 10-7-1982 for appearance before Martial Law authority and before the said date of appearance Kamal Uddin died by suffering serious mental agony; that thereafter on 9-6-1982 the prayer for mandatory injunction was incorporated as the defendants constructed house in some portion of the suit land during pendency of the suit by amending the plaint. 

 4. The defendant Nos. 1-5, 7-8 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint contending, inter alia, that the defendants have right, title and possession in 34 sataks of land in RS plot No. 1172 under RS khatian 615; that original owner of the suit land was Abdul Meah, who died leaving son Bazal Ahmed; that Majma Khatun; Bazal Ahmed died leaving behind wife Majma Khatun, who married Rashid Ahmed and both of them used to live in the domain of Bazal Ahmed as husband and wife; that Rashid Ahmed, Majma Khatun gave birth one son Emdadul Islam, two daughters named Nurun Nahar and Shamsun Nahar; that the suit property was put to auction for arrear rents through CC No. 1937(A)-1946-47 and auction purchased by Syed Ahmed of Chakaria on 14-10-1947 and got possession through Court on 6-2-1978; Syed Ahmed after getting possession of the suit land died leaving behind 4 sons namely Jashim Uddin, Nasir Uddin, Monir Uddin, Hasan Ahmed and one wife namely, Sajeda Begum; that the heirs of Syed Ahmed instituted Misc. Case No. 106/63-64 before the CO Revenue for demarcation of the property of RS plot No. 1172 corresponding to PS plot No. 438; that during preparation of PS record the name of one Abdul Bashar was wrongly recorded with Syed Ahmed and the heirs of Syed Ahmed by filing Appeal No. 45/62 corrected their names and accordingly their names were inserted; that the plaintiffs and their vendors cannot claim any title in the suit land as their right was extinguished through auction sale in 1946; that the transfer deeds shown by the plaintiffs are false and fraudulent and those were not acted upon; that Jasimuddin and others transferred the property of suit plot No. 1172 to the defendants by executing 7 deeds dated 1-8-1980 and delivered possession; that the defendants duly paid revenue and taxes to the Government; that the suit property was basically a tank and the heirs of Syed Ahmed by earth filling developed the land into vhiti land and the defendants erected two katcha house in the northern side; that on 20-8-1980 while the plaintiffs broken the said 2 katcha house, the defendant filed Panchalis Police Station Case No. 16(8)80 and before institution of the present suit the defendants erected a katcha house in southern side of the suit land; that the plaintiffs amalgamated RS plot No. 1173 with RS plot No. 1172; that the plaintiffs have no right title and possession in the suit land; that the defendant Nos. 1, 2, 4-7 filed an additional written statement stating, inter alia, that the facts alleged in the application for amendment of plaint are not correct; that the defendant did not influence Martial Law authority during continuation of Martial Law regime; that the cause of Martial Law harassment to the predecessor of plaintiffs by defendants by issuance of notices are not correct. The plaintiffs filed the suit on false averments and, as such, the suit is liable to be dismissed. 

 9. Mr Omar Faruk, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-petitioners in the course of argument takes me through the plaint, exhibited document, judgments of 2 Courts below and other materials on record and then submits that the plaintiff purchased the suit property by 5 registered deeds being registered deed dated 23-3-1978 , 8-2-1979 , 9-2-1979, 10-12-1979 and 11-12-1979 (Exhibited documents.) and since the date of purchase the plaintiffs have been possessing the suit land by paying rent to the Government in accordance with law although during pendency' of the suit the defendants with some miscreants forcibly dispossessed the plaintiffs on 18-1-1981 from the suit land although the Court of appeal below without considering the fact that during pendency of the suit the defendants forcibly dispossessed the plaintiffs from the suit land most illegally set-aside the well founded judgment of the trial Court below, which resulted in the failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiffs to prove his case examined 3 witnesses out of which PW 1, PW 2 and PW 3 in their respective evidence categorically stated that the plaintiffs are the real owner of the suit land and they possessed the suit land. Finally, the learned Advocate submits that the plaintiffs to prove their right, title and possession in the suit land exhibited a series of documents namely, Exhibit 1 (RS khatian No. 615), Exhibit 1 (a) (RS khatian No. 681), Exhibit 2 (dakhila of original owner), Exhibit 2(a), 2(b)-(rent receipt of original owner of khatian No. 615), Exhibit 2(c), 2(d), 2(e)-(rent receipt of original owner of khatian No. 681), Exhibit 3 (Certificate Objection Case No. 3496/ 60-61), Exhibit 4 to 4(k) (deeds) etc. although the Court of appeal below giving a goby to such material evidence on record abruptly arrived at a finding that the plaintiffs could not prove their prima-facie title and possession in the suit land. The learned Advocate to fortify his submission has relied on the decision reported in 48 DLR (AD) 75.
